title: weekday-vs-weekend-microburst-latency-cost-heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch to capture heuristic differences in microburst behavior between weekday traffic and weekend traffic and the downstream implications for p90/p99 latency SLOs and $/query. The goal is to produce a short set of heuristic rules product and runtime teams can use when deciding: slot sizing, burst capacity reservation, and short-window autoscaling thresholds.

Key takeaways (quick):
- Weekdays show heavier, correlated microbursts tied to user session starts (09:00–18:00 local) with higher sustained short-term slot contention. This increases p99 by ~15–40% for small-session conversational use-cases compared with weekends.
- Weekends have fewer but taller isolated bursts (higher peak QPS) driven by batch/analytics customers; they create short-term preemption pressure but lower sustained latency penalty if prefetch/kv cache hitrate is good.
- Operational heuristics: prefer slightly larger slot reservations (5–10%) during weekday business hours for mid-tier customers; prefer burst-admission backoff + aggressive prefetch on weekends.

Methodology (sketch):
- Dataset: 14-day sampled traces from prod-obsv (Apr 18–May 01 2026), sessionized by client_request_id.
- Cohorts: consumer-app sessions (interactive chat, median tokens 120) vs. analytics-batch (embedding jobs, median tokens 800).
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), CPU/GPU slot occupancy (%), KV cache hitrate, requests/sec (RPS), and cost-delta (in $ per 10k requests using internal cost model).
- Sampling: sampled all sessions with >1 token generation and grouped into 15-minute windows. For burst identification used a simple local-peak detector (window size=3, threshold multiplier=2.5 on baseline).

Summary tables (text / ascii):
1) Microburst frequency & shape (weekday vs weekend, interactive cohort)

+----------------------+------------+------------+------------+
| window type          | bursts/day | median h/s | 90th h/s   |
+----------------------+------------+------------+------------+
| Weekday (Mon–Fri)    | 142        | 1.6x       | 3.8x       |
| Weekend (Sat–Sun)    | 47         | 2.4x       | 6.2x       |
+----------------------+------------+------------+------------+

Notes: bursts/day = count of detected local peaks per day (interactive cohort). median h/s = median height/steady baseline ratio; 90th h/s = 90th percentile height/steady baseline ratio. Weekdays: more frequent but lower height. Weekends: rarer but spikeier.

2) Latency & cost snapshot (per 10k requests, interactive cohort)

+----------------------+----------+----------+-----------+
| scenario             | p90 ms   | p99 ms   | $ / 10k   |
+----------------------+----------+----------+-----------+
| Weekday baseline     | 210      | 410      | 3.8       |
| Weekday burst window | 260      | 560      | 5.1       |
| Weekend baseline     | 195      | 360      | 3.6       |
| Weekend peak window  | 230      | 620      | 6.0       |
+----------------------+----------+----------+-----------+

Interpretation: weekday bursts inflate p99 moderately (more tail mass) and increase short-term $/10k due to extra preemptions and slot allocations. Weekend peaks produce higher p99 in extreme windows because of taller spikes and lower cache warmup.

3) KV cache hitrate & tail coupling (weekday interactive cohort)
- Baseline hitrate: 68% weekdays, 74% weekends.
- During bursts: hitrate drops ~8 p.p. weekdays, ~12 p.p. weekends (cache churn + cold starts).
- Heuristic: pre-warm TTL increase of small prefix caches during predicted weekend windows reduces weekend p99 by ~18% in offline sim (see linked PR for sim config).

Short ASCII sparkline of sample 3-hour burst (representative):
time:    00:00 00:15 00:30 00:45 01:00 01:15 01:30 01:45 02:00 02:15 02:30
RPS:     _/\___/\____/\_____/\_____/\__\_____ /\_  (peak ~12x baseline)
lat p99: 100 120 150 180 400 520 480 230 160 130 110

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Is the local-peak detector too sensitive to small oscillations? We need to compare with a convolutional smoothing detector. TODO: run on May 01–May 14 range and compare.
- Cost model sensitivity: current $/10k uses amortized GPU hour cost and excludes network egress for embeddings-heavy cohorts. Need an adjusted cost bucket for mixed workloads.
- Slack/alerting: should we create a weekday burst alert that triggers a temporary slot increase policy? Concern: oscillation loops. Proposed: a 3-min dampening and require sustained 5-min above-barrier.

Suggested heuristics (concrete):
1) Business-hours weekday heuristic (09:00–18:00 local):
   - Reserve +5% slots for mid-tier plans (applies to hosts with >100 RPS baseline).
   - Set prefetch aggression to medium; avoid aggressive prefetch that evicts long-tail KV entries.
   - SLO gating: escalate to canary fallback at 30% p99 degradation over baseline for 10 minutes.

2) Weekend peak heuristic:
   - Allow higher transient admission but enable best-effort fallbacks (compress outputs) for low-tier customers.
   - Increase lightweight prefix cache TTLs for 4 hour windows around historical peaks.

3) Sampling & instrumentation suggestions:
   - Increase microburst sampling granularity from 15m->5m windows for the interactive cohort during weekends for 2-week trial.
   - Instrument per-tenant KV eviction rate in the traces; correlate per-tenant eviction spikes to p99.

Appendix: quick reproduction steps (for Eng SRE playbook)
1) GitHub: checkout perf-bench/weekday-weekend-experiments branch (linked artifact).
2) Reproduce: run ./bench.sh --cohort interactive --days 14 --peak-detector local-peak --threshold 2.5
3) Validation: compare p99 series with and without increased prefix cache TTL; generate ASCII tables using tools/awk/generate-summaries.py

Notes to self / next actions:
- Diego: please run convolutional detector comparison and drop results into CONFLUENCE-OBS-3912 by EOD 2026-05-14.
- Elena: simulate weekend-prefetch TTL change across a 1-node staging slice and capture kv hitrates.
- Product: discuss whether to expose a "weekend burst mode" in Redwood Console as an opt-in toggle for customers who prefer lower baseline $/q in exchange for occasional degraded p99.

References & links:

- Confluence notes: CONFLUENCE-OBS-3912 (microburst weekend study)
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-1427 (weekend prefetch sim ticket)

This is intentionally a rough notebook. Goal is to 1) capture the observed differences in microburst morphology between weekdays and weekends; 2) propose safe operational heuristics that reduce oscillation risk; and 3) highlight instrumentation gaps.
